text: κυρία, a lady: voc. my lady, an address of courtesy.

κυριακός (dominicus), of the Lord (κύριος), special to the Lord: δεῖπνον, supper (dinner) for church members, combined with the Eucharist: ἡμέρα, Sunday (cf. Fr. dimanche, Span. domingo, Ital. domenica). [In constitutional law means imperial.]
gloss: of the Lord (κύριος), special to the Lord

text: κυριεύω, I rule; c. gen. I rule over, lord it over, master.
κυριότης, (a) abstr., lordship, 2 Pet. ii 10; (b) concr., divine or angelic lordship, domination, dignity, Eph. i 21, Col. i 16, Jude 8, usually with reference to a celestial hierarchy.
κυρόω, I ratify, confirm.
κύων, a dog: universally despised in the East, and thus the name is applied contemptuously to persons, Phil. iii 2, Rev. xxii 15 (cf. Mt. xv 26).
κῶλον (membrum), a limb: plur. (membra) bodies.
κωμόπολις, a city which in constitution has only the status of a village.
gloss: a city which in constitution has only the status of a village

text: κῶμος (comissatio), a revel, a revelling, such as took place at the gathering of the grapes.
κώνωψ, a gnat, mosquito, referred to proverbially as something small.
Κῶς, Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, SW. of Asia Minor.
gloss: Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, SW. of Asia Minor

text: Κωσάμ (Hebr.), Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addei.
gloss: Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addei

text: λαγχάνω, (a) I obtain (receive) by lot, my lot (turn) is; (b) I cast lots, John xix 24.
gloss: I obtain (receive) by lot, my lot (turn) is

text: λάθρα (λάθρᾳ), secretly.
λαῖλαψ, a sudden storm, a squall.
λακτίζω, I kick.
λαλιά, (in classical Greek babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech.
Λάμεχ (Hebr.), Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah.
gloss: Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah

text: λαμπάς, a lamp, a lantern.
λαμπρός, shining, glossy, bright.
λαμπρότης, brightness.
λαμπρῶς, sumptuously.
λάμπω, I shine.
λαξευτός, hewn out of the rock.
Λαοδίκεια, Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia, near Colossae and Hierapolis.
gloss: Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia

text: Λαοδικεύς, a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea.
gloss: a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea

text: λάρυγξ, the throat.
Λασέα, another spelling of Λασαία, Lasaea, a city in Crete, about the middle of the S. coast.
note: Souter's headword is Λασέα (with Λασαία given as another spelling); the OCR had mismatched this target to λάσκω.

text: λατομέω, I hew (of stone).
λατρεία, service rendered to God, perhaps simply worship.
λάχανον, a vegetable.
λεγιών (Latin, = legio), properly a division of the Roman army, numbering about 6,000 infantry with additional cavalry (cf. Mt. xxvi 53): hence, a very large number.
gloss: properly a division of the Roman army

text: λεῖμμα, a remnant, a remainder.
λεῖος, smooth.

λείπω (earlier, I leave behind, abandon), (a) I am wanting; τὰ λείποντα, what is defective, Tit. i 5; (b) mid. e.g. c. gen. I come behind (in a race), I am left behind in, I fall short of (some standard), I am wanting in.

λειτουργέω, I act in the public service, I render service, I minister, in the widest sense, Rom. xv 27, of some special public religious service, Ac. xiii 2: but also of the service of priests and levites, Heb. x 11.
gloss: I act in the public service, I render service, I minister

text: λειτουργία, public service in the widest sense, 2 Cor. ix 12, Phil. ii 30: service as of priest or levite ritual, Lk. i 23, Phil. ii 17, Heb. viii 6, ix 21.
gloss: public service in the widest sense

text: λειτουργικός, given to serving (ministration), ministering.
λεμά (Aramaic), why.
λεντίον (Latin, = linteum), a towel.
note: Souter prints the headword accented λεντίον.

text: λεπίς, a scale, a scaly substance thrown off from the body.
λέπρα, leprosy.
λεπρός, a leprous person, a leper.
λεπτόν, a small piece of money, probably the smallest piece of money = ½ quadrans (κοδράντης, which see).

Λευεί, Λευείς (Hebr.), Levi, (a) an ancestor of Jesus, Lk. iii 24; (b) another ancestor of Jesus, Lk. iii 29; (c) third son of Jacob, the patriarch, and founder of a tribe named after him, Heb. vii 5, 9, Rev. vii 7; (d) son of Alphaeus, and called also Matthew, a revenue officer and one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
note: Souter's headword spelling is Λευεί, Λευείς.

text: λευείτης, a levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi; hence, a priest’s assistant, an under priest, as the members of that tribe were charged with this duty.
gloss: a levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi

text: λευειτικός, belonging to the tribe of Levi, levitical.
gloss: belonging to the tribe of Levi, levitical

text: λευκαίνω, I whiten.
λέων, a lion: ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Ἰούδα applied to Jesus, Rev. v 5 (after Gen. xlix 9): in 2 Tim. iv 17 used proverbially for very great danger.
λήθη, forgetfulness.
λῆμψις, receiving.
ληνός, a winepress: hence met. Rev. xiv 19, xix 15.
λῆρος, folly, nonsense, idle talk.
λίβανος (Semitic word), frankincense, incense.
λιβανωτός, a censer.
Λιβερτῖνος (Latin, = libertinus), a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves. A synagogue at Jerusalem appears to have been reserved for them.
gloss: a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves

text: Λιβύη, Libya, Africa (in the modern sense).
λιθάζω, I stone.
λίθινος, made of stone.
λιθόστρωτος, paved with stone.
λικμάω, I crush to powder.
λιμήν, a harbour, port.
λίνον, flax; linen.
Λίνος, Linus, a Christian in Rome.
λιπαρός, (lit. fat) rich, sumptuous.
λίτρα (libra), a Roman pound, of about twelve ounces, 327½ grammes.
gloss: a Roman pound, of about twelve ounces

text: λίψ (Africus), the south-west wind, and thus the quarter from which it comes.
λογεία, λογία (from λογεύω, ‘I collect’), a collection, collecting (of money), particularly of an irregular local contribution for religious purposes.
λογικός, (a) reasonable, rational, Rom. xii 1; (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with literal, 1 Pet. ii 2 (so perhaps also in Rom. xii 1).

λόγιον, plur. oracles, divine responses or utterances (it can include the entire O. T. scriptures); in Rom. iii 2 mainly of the promises in the Old Testament; in Heb. v 12 probably of Jesus’ teaching.
λόγιος, eloquent.
λογισμός, reasoning, thinking.
λογομαχέω, I battle with (for) words.
λογομαχία, a battling with (for) words, a battle of words.
gloss: a battling with (for) words, a battle of words

text: λόγχη, a long lance.
λοιδορέω, I revile a person to his face, I abuse insultingly.
gloss: I revile a person to his face, I abuse insultingly

text: λοιδορία, reviling, abuse.
λοίδορος, a railer, reviler, abuser.
λοιμός (pestis), (a) a pestilence; (b) a pestilent fellow, Ac. xxiv 5.

Λουκᾶς, Lucas, Luke, an abbreviated pet-form either of Λουκανός, as the Old Latin Bible gave in the title of the Third Gospel, or of Λούκιος, as some moderns have thought, Christian physician and writer of the Third Gospel and Acts.

Λούκιος, Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, Ac. xiii 1, by some identified with the evangelist Luke; (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a), Rom. xvi 21.
λουτρόν, a bath (of the water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing.
gloss: a bath (of the water, not the vessel), water for washing

text: λούω (literally or merely ceremonially), I wash, bathe (the body): mid. of washing, bathing one’s self.
Λύδδα, Lydda, Diospolis, Lod (modern Ludd), a city on the way to Joppa within a day’s journey of Jerusalem.
Λυδία, Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.
gloss: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi

text: Λυκαονία, Lycaonia; the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities Derbe and Lystra.
note: Punctuation after Lycaonia is faint: read as a semicolon, but it may be a comma (if a comma, gloss could be "Lycaonia, the country of the Lykaones").

text: Λυκαονιστί, in the Lycaonian language.
Λυκία, Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
gloss: Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor

text: λύκος, a wolf, or perhaps a jackal: often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities.
gloss: a wolf, or perhaps a jackal

text: λυμαίνομαι, I ravage, harry, devastate.
Λυσανίας, Lysanias, tetrarch of Abilene.
Λυσίας, Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.
gloss: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem

text: λύσις, dissolution, release.
λυσιτελέω, impers. 3 sing. it is advantageous to, it profits.
gloss: it is advantageous to, it profits
note: Souter's headword is λυσιτελέω (the lemma λυσιτελεῖ is its impersonal 3 sing.).

text: Λύστρα, Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.
λύτρον, the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom, the price of ransoming; especially the sacrifice by which expiation is effected, an offering of expiation.
gloss: the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom

text: λυτρόω (originally, I deliver captives from robbers or enemies in war by payment, I manumit or liberate a slave from slavery), I ransom, liberate, deliver.
note: Souter's headword is the active λυτρόω.

text: λύτρωσις (in O. T. ransoming from imprisonment for debt, or from slavery, release from national misfortune, &c.), liberation, deliverance, release (cf. λυτρόω).
λυτρωτής, a ransomer, a liberator.
Λωίς, Lois, grandmother of Timothy.
Λώτ (Λώθ) (Hebr.), Lot, nephew of Abraham.
Μαάθ (Hebr.), Maath, Mahath, an ancestor of Jesus.
gloss: Maath, Mahath, an ancestor of Jesus

text: Μαγαδάν, Magadan. The reading and the site are uncertain. Two views are held with regard to the latter, (a) that it was in the Decapolis near Gerasa; (b) that it was at Meğdel on the western bank of the Sea of Galilee.
note: The diacritic over the g in "Meğdel" is unclear (breve or similar mark); transcribed as ğ.

text: μαγία, sorcery, magic.
μάγος, a sorcerer, a magician, a wizard.
gloss: a sorcerer, a magician, a wizard

text: Μαγώγ (Hebr.), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in O.T. (Gen. x 2, Ezek. xxxviii 2, xxxix 6), probably the Scythians; hence, used in apocalyptic literature.
gloss: Magog, sometimes as name of a people

text: Μαδιάμ (Hebr.), Madiam, Midian, generally taken to mean or to include the peninsula of Sinai.
μαθητεύω, I make disciples, I make into disciples: followed by dat. of instrument, Mt. xiii 52.
gloss: I make disciples, I make into disciples

text: μαθήτρια, a woman disciple.
Μαθθαῖος, Matthaeus, Matthew, a revenue officer, then one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
Μαθθάτ (Ματθάτ) (Hebr.), Matthat, son of Levi and father of Jorem, an ancestor of Jesus.
gloss: Matthat, son of Levi and father of Jorem

text: Μαθθίας, Matthias, elected one of the Twelve in room of the deceased Judas.
gloss: Matthias, elected one of the Twelve

text: Μαθουσάλα (Hebr.), Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech.
gloss: Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech

text: μαίνομαι (furo), I am raving mad, I speak as a madman.
gloss: I am raving mad, I speak as a madman

text: μακαρίζω, I deem (declare) happy.
μακαρισμός, felicitation, regarding as happy or enviable.
gloss: felicitation, regarding as happy or enviable

text: Μακεδών, a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia.
gloss: a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia

text: μάκελλον (Latin, = macellum), meat-market.
μακροθύμως, with long-suffering, patiently.
μακροχρόνιος, long-timed, long-lived.
μαλακία (malacia), weakness, illness.
μαλακός (mollis), (a) soft, (τὰ) μαλακά, as substantive, soft material; (b) of persons, soft, voluptuous, effeminate (really = cinaedus, pathicus).
Μαλελεήλ (Hebr.), Maleleel, Malelehel, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Maleleel, Malelehel, one of the ancestors of Jesus

text: Μάλχος (Aram. Malchu), Malchus, a slave of the high-priest at Jerusalem.
gloss: Malchus, a slave of the high-priest at Jerusalem
note: "high-priest" is broken at a line end after the hyphen; unclear whether the hyphen is real (kept as high-priest).

text: μάμμη, a grandmother.
μαμωνᾶς (Aramaic, with cognate words in Hebrew and Punic), riches, money, possessions, property.
Μαναήν (grecized form of Aramaic Menahem), Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas’ court.
gloss: Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas’ court

text: Μανασσῆς (Hebr.), Manasseh, (a) son of Joseph, founder of a tribe of Israel, Rev. vii 6; (b) son of Hezekiah and father of Amon (Amos).
μανία (furor), raving madness.
μάννα (Hebrew), manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites in the desert: of spiritual food, Rev. ii 17.
gloss: manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites

text: μαντεύομαι, I practise soothsaying, suggesting the fraud involved in the practice.
μαραίνω: pass. I die, I wither (like the grass).
note: Souter's headword is the active μαραίνω (pass. sense given).

text: μαρὰν ἀθά (Aramaic), either Our Lord hath come, or Our Lord cometh (will come, is at hand).
gloss: Our Lord hath come, or Our Lord cometh
note: Souter prints the headword as two words, μαρὰν ἀθά.

text: μαργαρίτης (margarita), a pearl.
Μᾶρκος, Marcus, Mark, who also had the Hebrew name John, son of Mary [(c) above], nephew of Barnabas, coadjutor of Barnabas, Saul (Paul), and Peter.
μάρμαρος (marmor), marble.
μαρτύρομαι, (properly, I call (summon) to witness, and then, absolutely) I testify, I protest, I asseverate; (obtestor) I conjure, solemnly charge, 1 Thess. ii 12, Eph. iv 17.
gloss: I testify, I protest, I asseverate

text: μασάομαι, I gnaw.
μαστιγόω (uerbero), I flog, scourge, the victim being strapped to a pole or frame, see μάστιξ.
μαστίζω, I flog, scourge, see μάστιξ.
μάστιξ (flagrum), (a) a scourge, lash, of leathern thongs with pieces of metal sewn up in them, Ac. xxii 24, Heb. xi 36; (b) met. severe pains (sufferings) sent by God.
μαστός, a breast, especially a nipple of a woman’s breast.
ματαιολογία, vain speaking, foolish talking.
ματαιολόγος, speaking vain things.
ματαιόομαι, I am made vain, ineffective, godless.
gloss: I am made vain, ineffective, godless

text: μάταιος, vain, unreal, ineffectual, unproductive: practically godless.
ματαιότης, vanity, emptiness, unreality, purposelessness, ineffectiveness, instability.
μάτην, in vain, in an unreal way.
gloss: in vain, in an unreal way

text: Μαθθάν (Hebr.), Matthan, son of Eleazar and father of Jacob, an ancestor of Jesus.
gloss: Matthan, son of Eleazar and father of Jacob
note: Found on page 157 under Souter's spelling Μαθθάν (Matthan, Mt. i 15). The OCR had matched this target to the page-160 entry "Ματθάτ (Hebr.), Matthat, an ancestor of Jesus.", which is a different name (Matthat).

text: Ματταθά (Hebr.), Mattathah, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ματταθίας (Hebr.), Mattathias, an ancestor of Jesus.
μάχη, (earlier, a battle, conflict, perhaps in James iv 1; hence) in the sphere of words, &c., strife, contention, quarrel.
μάχομαι, I engage in battle, I fight: hence I strive, John vi 52.
gloss: I engage in battle, I fight

text: μεγαλεῖος: τὰ μεγαλεῖα (magnalia), the mighty deeds.
μεγαλειότης, (divine) majesty or magnificence.
μεγαλοπρεπής, magnificent, superb, transcendent.
μεγαλύνω, (a) I enlarge, lengthen, Mt. xxiii 5; (b) I increase, magnify.
μεγάλως, greatly: compar. μεῖζον.
μεγαλωσύνη, (divine) majesty; in Heb. i 3, viii 1, a sort of substitute for the divine Name.
μέγεθος, greatness.
μεγιστάν (megistan), a great one, a lord, a courtier, a satrap. (The word has an oriental flavour and belongs to late Greek.)
gloss: a great one, a lord, a courtier, a satrap

text: μέγιστος (elative superlative, practically obsolete and only literary), very great: see μέγας (positive), μείζων (comparative and superlative).
μεθερμηνεύω, I translate (from one language into another).
gloss: I translate (from one language into another)

text: μέθη, deep drinking, drunkenness.
μεθοδεία (from μέθοδος, a way of search after something, an inquiry; a method), scheming, craftiness.
μεθύσκομαι, I become intoxicated with wine, I become drunk.
gloss: I become intoxicated with wine, I become drunk

text: μέθυσος (originally, tipsy), a drunkard.
μεθύω, I am intoxicated with wine, I am drunk.
gloss: I am intoxicated with wine, I am drunk

text: μειζότερος, μείζων, (a) compar. greater (3 John 4); (b) superl. greatest, Mt. xiii 32, xxiii 11, 1 Cor. xiii 13, &c.
μέλας, black: τὸ μέλαν (atramentum), ink, 2 Cor. iii 3, 2 John 12, 3 John 13.
Μελεά (Hebr.), Meleah, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Meleah, one of the ancestors of Jesus

text: μελετάω, I devise, plan; practise, exercise myself in.
μέλι, honey.
Μελίτη (Μελιτήνη), Malta.
